evidence.excerpt: Power delivery network (PDN) impedance management in mixed-signal boards is examined through a combined measurement and simulation campaign. A test vehicle carrying an FPGA and two 12-bit ADC devices was designed with three decoupling capacitor placement strategies: bulk capacitors only, distributed 100 nF ceramic capacitors at 5 mm spacing, and a co-planar interdigitated capacitance structure formed by alternating power and ground copper pours. PDN impedance was measured from 100 kHz to 1 GHz using a one-port shunt method with a vector network analyser. Simultaneously, conducted noise on the 3.3 V rail was recorded with a 1 GHz oscilloscope probe during switching activity driven by a test pattern generator. The distributed ceramic strategy reduced peak PDN impedance from 840 mΩ to 210 mΩ at 480 MHz. Radiated emissions pre-compliance scans at 3 m confirmed a corresponding 4.8 dB reduction in broadband noise floor between 400 and 600 MHz. A compact circuit model of the PDN, fitted to measurement data, reproduces impedance to within 8% across the full bandwidth.
